answer: Admissions open along a curve rather than a gate. The first newcomer at the vertex in an epoch pledges one unit of the emission it has not yet earned, the second pledges four, the third nine, and the j-th pledges j squared, deducted from that seat's first twenty epochs of income and carrying an equal deduction of voting weight. A lantern of ten aliases assembled in a single epoch therefore forfeits 385 units of both earnings and standing, while one latecomer on the tide into harbor forfeits a single unit, and the bill cannot be split because each admission lifts the price demanded of the next.
